commit_message:
curl: implement non-blocking STDIN read on Windows

Implements a seperate read thread for STDIN on Windows when curl is run
with -T/--upload-file .

This uses a similar technique to the nmap/ncat project, spawning a
seperate thread which creates a loop-back bound socket, sending STDIN
into this socket, and reading from the other end of said TCP socket in a
non-blocking way in the rest of curl.

Fixes #17451
Closes #17572

fix_commit_message:
curl: tool_read_cb fix of segfault

When transfers read client input without an upload file, the check if
upload file is '.' strcompared a NULL.

Add test 1548 to reproduce and verify fix.

Reported-by: d1r3ct0r
Fixes #17978
Closes #17987
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 9657a2041e77 on top of intro 9a2663322c33 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): The curl command-line tool's read callback (tool_read_cb in src/tool_cb_rea.c) was modified to support non-blocking STDIN reads on Windows when the user specifies `-T .` (upload from stdin). The added branch determines whether this special-case logic applies by comparing `per->uploadfile` to the string "." using strcmp(). However, per->uploadfile can legitimately be NULL for transfers that invoke the read callback without an associated upload file (e.g., certain non-upload transfers that still supply data via the read callback). Because the code failed to check for NULL before calling strcmp(), such transfers trigger a NULL pointer dereference and crash (segfault). Root cause: Missing NULL check before calling strcmp() on a pointer (per->uploadfile) that is not guaranteed to be non-NULL in all code paths that reach tool_read_cb().
